I built a consumer-lending SaaS alone and ran it for over a decade. It did what
most one-person projects don't: it drew media coverage, passed 10,000 customers,
and stayed profitable the whole way. Running it solo for that long is its own
kind of engineering. Every choice was mine to live with, and the discipline was
knowing which corners were safe to cut and which would bite later. The clearest
proof is that it survived three major Rails upgrades over its life and never
stopped for a rewrite, because the code stayed simple enough to carry forward.
